key_insight: Learning to sample from an unknown reward-induced Gibbs distribution can achieve logarithmic-in-time sampling regret, unlike the typical square-root scaling of classical regret.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers theoretical guidance for balancing output diversity and reward in entropy-regularized RL, RLHF, and reward-guided generation.
method: Define sampling regret using temperature-normalized cumulative KL divergence to the Gibbs target.
Develop UCS and TS², sampling analogues of UCB and Thompson sampling.
Bound regret through squared confidence widths and posterior-random Gibbs distributions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical regret decompositions and logarithmic guarantees in standard settings at fixed temperature, but no empirical evaluation.
watch_item: Logarithmic guarantees are stated for fixed temperature in standard settings; they should not be assumed for arbitrary models or temperature schedules.
paper_title: The Tilted Sampling Problem: Optimism, Posterior Sampling, and Logarithmic Regret
